evals.prompt: I have a fuzzy product idea for saved layouts. Shape it into tracked work through our configured Orca loop.
evals.expected_output: Passes the setup readiness gate, revalidates the configured Alignment profile, waits for confirmation, then launches a single-use Alignment Agent with the complete request.
expectations: Reads docs/agents/orca-development-loop.md before bootstrapping or touching tickets
Uses the current host's configured Alignment profile from docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml rather than discovering a model
Waits for explicit confirmation before creating a Task or terminal
Creates the complete Task before launch
Inlines the user's request and asks the user to switch only after profile verification

evals.prompt: The mute toggle bug is bounded and its actual and expected behavior are precise. Make it ready for an agent.
evals.expected_output: Uses focused clarification and /to-tickets without forcing a spec, then verifies the configured tracker by Adapter readback.
expectations: Does not require /to-spec for one bounded bug
Recommends exactly one next user-invoked skill
Uses the configured Tracker Adapter rather than a remembered provider command
Completes only after tracker readback

evals.prompt: Deliver GH-42 and GH-43 through Orca. This repository's setup manifest certifies GitHub Issues as the primary tracker.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the certified GitHub Adapter, validates the tickets and dependency policy, revalidates configured role pools, and waits for wave confirmation.
expectations: Does not reject GitHub because it is not Linear
Uses operation templates from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
Reads validation only from docs/agents/environment.md
Uses user-supplied certified profiles
Freezes the Adapter revision in the Wave Manifest
Freezes complete definitions for every role-bound profile

evals.prompt: Kick off delivery for ITEM-201. There is no docs/agents/orca-development-loop.md in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Stops at the setup readiness gate and gives /setup-orca-development-loop as the one recovery action.
expectations: Creates no Run, Task, handoff, terminal, or worktree
Does not fall back to package scripts or tracker guessing
Does not mention setup-matt-pocock-skills as the setup path
Names /setup-orca-development-loop

evals.prompt: Shape this feedback into tickets. Our setup says the tracker is execution-only because it cannot create work items.
evals.expected_output: Stops Alignment on its readiness capability while preserving the ability to execute existing approved tickets.
expectations: Does not invent a create command
Explains the missing Alignment capability
Does not mark Execution blocked merely because Alignment is blocked
Points to setup if the user wants to change integrations

evals.prompt: Deliver ITEM-101 then ITEM-102. The configured dependency mode is user-attestation-required because neither the tracker nor an alternate representation can be read. I gave you the order, but ITEM-101 may also depend on an external ITEM-90.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to treat ordering as blocker evidence and requires a complete per-ticket blocker attestation including ITEM-90 and its satisfaction before any launch.
expectations: Separates AFK-ready role from launchability
Does not accept ITEM-101 then ITEM-102 as proof of blocker completeness
Requires the complete blocker set for every ticket, including external blockers
Requires ITEM-90's current satisfaction and an exact user confirmation reference
Freezes the exact user confirmation as completeness evidence
Excludes a ticket whose external blocker is unsatisfied
Creates no Coordinator handoff before the evidence is complete

evals.prompt: Start ITEM-101 and ITEM-102 using our usual profiles. The repo was set up yesterday on this host.
evals.expected_output: Revalidates only configured entries, reads headroom fresh, presents the exact pools and capacity, and waits for confirmation.
expectations: Reads the current host binding and certification from docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml
Does not enumerate all models, agents, accounts, or executables
Reads current headroom rather than a stored value
Shows maxParallelTickets and maxConcurrent
Requires per-wave confirmation
Copies every referenced profile into the manifest rather than leaving mutable repository lookups

evals.prompt: Use model Z instead of every configured Worker profile for this wave.
evals.expected_output: Treats the user-supplied model as a one-wave override, validates only it, and does not edit long-lived profile configuration.
expectations: Does not silently persist the override
Validates the exact agent/model/reasoning and launch path
Records profilesSource as one-wave-override
Requires a revised manifest and confirmation

evals.prompt: ITEM-103's pinned worker provider is exhausted, but another certified Worker profile in the manifest pool is available.
evals.expected_output: Fails over inside the confirmed pool while preserving tier and cross-family review constraints.
expectations: Requires no new confirmation for in-pool failover
Records the provider error and substitution
Respects maxConcurrent and ticket tier
Keeps the Reviewer family different
Stops for confirmation if only an out-of-pool option remains

evals.prompt: The ITEM-104 reviewer requested changes. Reuse both agents for a fix and focused re-review.
evals.expected_output: Retains and re-dispatches both terminals in the same Issue Worktree with fresh lifecycle preambles and delta Tasks.
expectations: Re-dispatches the original Worker then Reviewer
Uses new Task and Dispatch IDs
Carries complete active findings and changed acceptance facts
Does not repeat stable role, tracker, profile, or project context
Keeps process outcome separate from review verdict

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. The implementation Worker reported a clean committed head and passing tests. Start review.
evals.expected_output: Performs metadata-only checks, retains the Worker, and dispatches a fresh independent Reviewer in the same worktree.
expectations: Checks lifecycle IDs, commit, HEAD, clean status, and base ancestry
Does not read the diff or issue an ACCEPT
Retains the Worker
Uses the pinned Reviewer profile
Leaves code-review and the verdict to the Reviewer

evals.prompt: ITEM-105 is accepted. Main advanced, but merge preflight reports no content conflicts.
evals.expected_output: Uses the existing Issue Worktree for a deterministic candidate and advances main only after validation and tree equivalence.
expectations: Takes the mutation lock
Creates no dedicated Integration Worktree
Uses current main as the first parent
Validates combined state in the Issue Worktree
Confirms main is unchanged before advancing it

evals.prompt: ITEM-106 is accepted, and non-mutating preflight reports content conflicts with main.
evals.expected_output: Creates a conflict-only Integration Worktree and requires an Integration Worker and fresh Integration Reviewer.
expectations: Runs non-mutating preflight first
Preserves accepted implementation evidence
Uses resolving-merge-conflicts
Requires a fresh Integration Reviewer
Advances main only after review and final validation

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. Your 15-minute wait timed out and two heartbeat cadences were missed.
evals.expected_output: Treats silence as a stall and climbs the bounded recovery ladder.
expectations: Runs worker-show and one bounded worker-read
Uses worker-stop or worker-abandon based on proof
Retries with worker-start --retry-of and durable artifacts
Blocks and escalates after two failed relaunches

evals.prompt: Stop the ITEM-110 wave; I changed my mind.
evals.expected_output: Runs user abort, leaves main and tracker lifecycle unchanged, preserves work, and reports every stopping point.
expectations: Main sends the stop to the Coordinator Run and waits for acknowledgement
Stops or fences live Dispatches
Posts no completion write to the tracker
Reports abandoned outcomes and retained resources

evals.prompt: You are the newly launched Alignment Agent. Main supplied complete feedback. Begin.
evals.expected_output: Applies the frozen effective-profile evidence, then responds with its values or limitation, a feedback summary, and one exact slash command before broad exploration.
expectations: Runs the configured read-only command only in attestation mode
Runs no profile probe in receipt or user-attested mode
First visible response includes the evidence mode and profile values or limitation
Summarizes all received feedback
Recommends exactly one slash skill
Does no broad repository or tracker exploration first

evals.prompt: You are the Alignment Agent. All six ticket slices still require structural decisions. Finish the session.
evals.expected_output: Reports unresolved structure or over-wide slices instead of manipulating the tier distribution.
expectations: Uses the configured complexity representation and anchors
Treats cross-module contracts as complex
Does not lift tiers merely because the parent feature was difficult
Keeps open-question tickets out of the ready manifest
Reports the all-high-tier signal

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator and your actual profile matches the Wave Manifest. Start the wave and report readiness.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the Adapter and profile, creates the Coordinator Run, then sends coordinator_ready as a subject on a valid Orca message type.
expectations: Creates no Run before setup and profile verification
Uses a valid --type
Carries coordinator_ready as subject
Addresses the Main Run explicitly
Includes Coordinator Run ID, manifest version, and Adapter revision

evals.prompt: The configured tracker integration now resolves to a different Orca project than the setup manifest.
evals.expected_output: Reports setup drift and stops without switching providers or rewriting configuration.
expectations: Distinguishes setup drift from temporary unavailability
Does not touch tickets
Does not pick another integration
Directs the user to /setup-orca-development-loop

evals.prompt: The wave integrated ITEM-120 successfully. Complete its tracker lifecycle and clean up.
evals.expected_output: Uses the configured Adapter to publish evidence, complete and de-queue the ticket, read it back, then release resources.

Applies the configured completed lifecycle and removes AFK-ready

Sweeps parents only when parent reads are certified

evals.prompt: Resume the already-active legacy wave. Its old frozen Wave Manifest still exists, but this repo has not run the new setup yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses the frozen manifest only to finish or stop the existing wave, creates no new work, and defers configuration migration until afterward.
expectations: Does not migrate the active wave
Does not add tickets or profiles
Uses the frozen tracker and profile facts for the existing wave
Requires /setup-orca-development-loop before a later new wave

evals.expected_output: Freezes one self-contained profile dictionary containing all five definitions and role bindings that reference them, so the Coordinator needs no mutable repository profile lookup.

Includes exact agent, model, reasoning, family, maxConcurrent, current headroom, launch recipes, and certification for iw1 and ir1

expectations: Does not treat one ticket as implicitly blocker-free
Requires an explicit complete-set attestation even when the set is empty

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. ITEM-140 has an accepted, validated candidate, but the durable main checkout has modified files and main is checked out there. Advance the base.

Runs git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain in the durable checkout

evals.expected_output: Leaves local main unchanged, pushes the accepted implementation branch without force, opens and reads back the PR, updates the ticket without completing it, and reports submitted.
expectations: Does not advance the local base ref
Treats the confirmed publication mode as push authority for only the configured branch and remote
Pushes the accepted implementation branch without force and reads back the canonical PR link

Detects that a touched ticket has a live Dispatch
Sends manifest_rejected as an escalation naming that check
Continues under version 2

evals.expected_output: Treats launch.effective from the start receipt as normative, verifies it against launch.requested, and runs no in-Task profile probe.
